time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame 0 at t = 0; time t -> frame round(t*24)
units: pixels and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.motion: static (frame 40 vs frame 0 outside the ball/shadow region: mean |diff| 0.13 grey levels; no pan, no shake)
camera.view: fixed camera looking at a plain grey studio backdrop: a lighter band (wall/backdrop) above a horizontal edge at y ~148 px, then a uniform grey surface with soft radial vignetting. The ball's shadow falls directly above it (frames 5-20) and then up and to the right (later frames), so the ball moves in front of this grey surface, which is not a perspective ground plane with markings. One pixel scale applies to the whole motion: the ball's apparent size is constant.

objects.name: ball
objects.description: soccer-style ball: light grey body with black star-shaped patches, specular highlight lower-left of centre. It is the only object in the scene.
objects.visible_frames: 4-40 (frame 4 partly beyond the left image border; fully visible 5-40; frames 0-3 empty)
objects.reference_point: sphere centre (= object origin); track columns cx, cy

size_px.note: The vertical diameter (top limb ~349.5, bottom limb ~415) is the true sphere diameter in pixels. Horizontally the sharp disc is also about 66 px across, but faint motion-blur smear widens the limb-to-limb extent to about 72-76 px. Use 66 px as the ball's pixel diameter (length = width = height for a sphere).

motion_summary_px.direction: left to right, horizontal; cy constant at 382.5 +/- 1 px (no vertical motion, no bounce)
motion_summary_px.per_frame_step_px: about 56-57 px/frame at frames 5-9, decreasing smoothly to about 45 px/frame at frames 36-40 (it slows down steadily); per-frame steps scatter +/-2 px

objects.shadow: large soft dark shadow attached to the top of the ball (y ~295-350), tilting up-right in later frames; it is not an object and was excluded from the ball's size

objects.name: backdrop_edge
objects.description: horizontal boundary between the lighter top band and the grey surface below
objects.note: spans the full width; it may be a wall/floor or backdrop fold. It is the only static feature; there are no markings or furniture.

events.event: ball enters the frame at the left edge (already moving)
ball passes the image centre x = 960
video ends with the ball still moving and fully visible (right limb ~1881 < 1919)

no_events: no release, bounce, impact, contact, stop or direction change is visible. Motion starts before frame 4 (off-screen) and continues past frame 40.

files.scripts/: all measurement scripts (track_ball.py is the final tracker)
